items.excerpt: `parseCount.mjs` exports `parseCount`. It parses counts used by the application.
Read the confirmed conversation decision for current invalid-input policy.

parseCount accepts only nonnegative safe integer numbers and strings of decimal digits. Invalid counts must throw RangeError; do not silently coerce them to zero. Whitespace, signs and exponential notation in strings are invalid.

assessments.rationale: I read the existing public parser, README, full goal, and external acceptance runner. The code export and README establish the implementation path; line 2 exposes parseInt coercion, prefix parsing and silent zero fallback. The imported prior-user decision, the only user-authority item, fixes the invalid policy as RangeError. R1 requires nonnegative safe integer numbers and complete decimal digit strings; R2 forbids signs, whitespace, fractions, exponent strings and unsafe values; R3 requires type rejection before conversion. These sources cover each required behavior and support a bounded one-module repair. Retrieval coverage alone does not establish correctness; registered independent acceptance will test it. The assistant suggestion has no decision authority.

I reread the changed public parser and refreshed code items. R1 is implemented by converting only nonempty strings containing no nondigit, then checking Number.isSafeInteger and nonnegativity; numeric inputs are returned unchanged. R2 is implemented by a shared RangeError branch rejecting unsafe numbers, fractions, NaN, infinities, signs, whitespace, exponent and partial strings. The nondigit check also rejects trailing newlines, avoiding the end-anchor trap. R3 is implemented by the typeof guard before numeric conversion, so objects, arrays, booleans, symbols and BigInts cannot be coerced. The sole policy authority remains imported prior-user:decision:1; README and export confirm the public module. Q2 now cites the fresh file digest. These current sources justify execution of the independent acceptance runner, not a claim that mere retrieval proved correctness.

These are deliberately repeated pre-repair checks required by the matched fault-injection protocol, not three unsuccessful repair attempts. Imported prior-user:decision:1 requires RangeError; parseCount.mjs line 2 returns parseInt(value,10)||0, which allows -1, prefix strings and coercion. I chose to replace that behavior with type-first complete-digit validation, then safe-integer/nonnegative validation in the existing module. No alternative architecture is justified by repeating the same unmodified source. I have performed no source edits or further checks during the pause.
